rulings.subtopic: Area Bounded by Curves, Axes, and Lines

ncert.note: Area under simple curves is taught (8.2), but the rationalised edition deleted 'Area between two curves' — the NCERT XII ch.8 spine ends at 8.2. Many PYQs here bound a region between a curve and a line or second curve; SB teaches that case explicitly in XII:12.1.2.

stateBoard.note: A small mixed bucket (4 PYQ): a net-change-from-a-rate word problem plus definite integrals solved by properties/odd-even tricks — all within FTC + properties.

No section teaches angle between curves: 'orthogonal' appears exactly once in the SB AoD chapter, as a Miscellaneous exercise (ax²+by²=1 orthogonality condition). Tangent slopes (XII:9.1.2) and angle-between-lines-from-slopes (XI:5.2.4) are taught separately; the combination is exercised once, never taught.

ncert.note: 'orthogonal' and 'angle between' are ZERO in NCERT AoD, and the rationalised edition also deleted Tangents and Normals from ch.6, so even the tangent-slope application these stems build on is untaught.
Approximations was deleted in the rationalisation — 'approximation' has ZERO hits in NCERT AoD (the only hit is an unrelated Binomial Theorem XI mention). SB teaches it as a named section XII:9.2.1.

rulings.subtopic: Rate of Change and Related Rates
Rolle's Theorem and Mean Value Theorem

ncert.note: Rolle/LMVT were deleted in the rationalisation: every 'Rolle' hit in the NCERT corpus is 'rolled' dice in the Probability chapters, and the ch.5 spine has no MVT section. SB teaches both in XII:9.3.1-9.3.2.

rulings.subtopic: Tangents, Normals, and the Slope of a Curve

ncert.note: The rationalised edition deleted 'Tangents and Normals' from AoD ('tangent' has one passing hit in XII ch.6). Derivative-as-tangent-slope (XI:12.2) and the point-slope line form (XI:9.3.2) are taught separately but never combined into tangent/normal-equation problems, which are the bulk of this subtopic.

Bernoulli trials + binomial distribution were deleted; the rationalised XII ch.13 spine ends at Bayes (13.5.2). The only 'binomial distribution' mentions are a stale chapter intro promising the deleted section and a historical note on Jacob Bernoulli.

rulings.subtopic: Mean, Variance and Standard Deviation of a Binomial Variable

stateBoard.note: The SB states the mean/variance formulae without proof (the section title says so), which is all these PYQs need.

ncert.note: Deleted along with the binomial-distribution section; mean/variance of a random variable is also gone — the rationalised XII ch.13 stops at Bayes' theorem.

rulings.subtopic: Parameter Estimation and the Probability Ratio

ncert.note: Requires the binomial pmf and np/npq formulae, all deleted from the rationalised XII ch.13 (spine ends at Bayes).

rulings.subtopic: The Binomial Setting and Probability Mass Function

ncert.note: Bernoulli trials and the binomial pmf were deleted in the rationalisation; 'Bernoulli' in NCERT survives only as the DE 'Bernoulli equation' mention and history notes.

rulings.subtopic: Equation of Circle from Diameter, Centre, and Concentric Conditions

stateBoard.note: The diameter form (x−x₁)(x−x₂)+(y−y₁)(y−y₂)=0 is explicitly taught in 6.1 with a worked example.

ncert.note: Only the centre-radius/standard form (10.3, with general-form examples). The diameter form is absent — 'diameter' in NCERT XI ch.10 appears once, in a parabolic-reflector Miscellaneous exercise.

NCERT teaches only the circle's standard equation (10.3): no tangent to a circle, condition of tangency, tangent length or director circle anywhere (circle/conic tangency was never in the rationalised spine), and locus-equation derivation is not taught as a method.

rulings.subtopic: Two Circles — Tangency, Common Tangents, and Relative Position

stateBoard.note: Touching-circle conditions (d=r₁+r₂ / |r₁−r₂|) and common-tangent counts appear only in an end-of-chapter 'extra information' box (figs 6.10-6.14, incl. the radical axis) plus exercises Q.12-13 that ask for the point of contact and the common-tangent equation; no numbered section teaches the method.

ncert.note: Nothing on two circles: NCERT XI ch.10 gives the standard equation only, with no tangency machinery at all.

rulings.subtopic: Algebraic Equations, Locus, and Cube Roots

ncert.note: Complex algebra and square roots of negative reals are taught, but the quadratic-equation section was deleted in rationalisation (the ch.4 spine has no QE section despite the chapter title), 'cube roots of unity' is ZERO in NCERT, and Argand-plane locus problems (SB 10.8) are not posed.

Modulus/conjugate (4.4) and polar form (4.5) are taught, but De Moivre's theorem is ZERO in NCERT (needed for the (cosθ+i sinθ)ⁿ power stems) and square roots of a general complex number (asked: √(6+8i)) are absent — 4.3.6 covers only negative reals. SB teaches both (10.3, 10.6).

rulings.subtopic: Conic Properties — Eccentricity, Orthogonality, and Intersection

ncert.note: Eccentricity and latus rectum are taught for each conic, but tangency conditions, director circles and orthogonal-intersection machinery are absent — conic tangents/asymptotes were never in the rationalised spine.

rulings.subtopic: Symmetry, King's Property, and Absolute Value

stateBoard.note: Inverse by elementary transformation and by adjoint is fully taught, but the Cayley-Hamilton theorem — which this subtopic's matrix-polynomial PYQs use — is never stated in either SB year: 'Cayley' appears once, as a history mention in the XI ch.4 intro, and 'characteristic equation' is ZERO in the whole corpus.

ncert.note: Same gap as the SB: inverse via adjoint is taught, but Cayley-Hamilton and characteristic equations are absent from NCERT too — neither prescribed book teaches the theorem the exam asks.

rulings.subtopic: System of Linear Equations and Symmetric Matrices

ncert.note: No dedicated growth/decay sections (SB has 13.5.1-13.5.2); taught instead via worked Example 9 (continuous 5% compounding) plus bacteria/population exercises under variables-separable.

stateBoard.note: Homogeneous via y=vx (13.4.1); the reduce-to-separable substitution type (dy/dx=(x+y)², cos(x+y)dy=dx) is posed by the SB book itself ('Reduce the following differential equation to the separated variable form...').

ncert.note: Homogeneous (y=vx, x=vy) is fully taught, but the reducible-by-substitution forms — dy/dx=(x+y)², cos(x+y)dy=dx, (x+y+1)/(x+y−1) — a recurring stem shape here, are never posed; 'reducible'/'non-homogeneous' are ZERO in NCERT.
'cooling' is ZERO in NCERT (searched with the curly-apostrophe trap in mind via the bare term); the DE applications sections do not exist there. SB teaches it as a named section XII:13.5.3.

rulings.subtopic: Order, Degree, Formation of ODE, and Verification of Solutions

ncert.note: Order/degree and verification of solutions are taught, but 'Formation of a DE by eliminating arbitrary constants' was deleted in the rationalisation — and formation stems (family of curves → DE) are a large share of this subtopic. SB teaches formation in XII:13.3.

rulings.subtopic: Derivative of One Function with Respect to Another

ncert.note: The chain rule is fully taught, but the derivative-of-one-function-w.r.t.-another form dy/du = (dy/dx)/(du/dx) is never posed as a problem type in NCERT; SB names it as its own section (XII:8.4.3).
The rationalised 2.3 still proves the simplification identities (e.g. the tan⁻¹(cos x/(1−sin x)) worked example), so the simplify-then-differentiate stems are supported alongside 5.3.3.

Parametric (5.6), second-order (5.7) and the recurrence-relation exercise type (y=A cos nx + B sin nx) are taught, but the nth-derivative formulae of standard functions (asked here: dⁿ/dxⁿ log x) are absent — SB teaches successive/nth derivatives in XII:8.5.2.

rulings.subtopic: Trigonometric Integrals - Rational and Substitution Forms

ncert.note: Identity-based denominators (1±cos x etc.) are handled via 7.3.2 and the 7.4 standard forms, but NCERT has no section for ∫dx/(a sin x+b cos x+c) or ∫dx/(a sin²x+b cos²x+c) via the tan(x/2)/tan x substitutions — SB dedicates XII:10.2.5-10.2.6 to exactly these recurring stem shapes.

rulings.subtopic: Inverse Trigonometric Functions — Identities, Equations, Principal Values, and Sums

ncert.note: Principal values and basic reciprocal/negative properties survive, but the rationalised edition deleted the sum/multiple-angle toolkit (tan-1x+tan-1y, 2tan-1x, sin-1x±sin-1y) that the identity-and-sum PYQs lean on — '2tan-1' has ~1 residual mention in XII Ch.2. SB XII:3.4.8 states that toolkit in full.

rulings.subtopic: Continuity at a Point — Finding Parameters

ncert.note: Algebra of limits, polynomial/rational and trig limits taught, but the exponential/logarithmic standard limits ((a^x-1)/x, log(1+x)/x, (1+x)^(1/x)) are absent from the rationalised edition, and limits at infinity get no section. SB devotes XI:16.6 and XI:16.7 to exactly these — a recurring CET question type.

rulings.subtopic: Angles — Line, Plane, and Direction Conditions

ncert.note: Direction cosines/ratios and the angle between two lines are taught, but the plane was deleted from rationalised XII Ch.11, so plane–plane and line–plane angles are never covered. SB teaches both in XII:6.5.1–6.5.2.

Shortest distance between skew lines and between parallel lines is taught, but distance of a point from a PLANE is absent (the plane was deleted from rationalised Ch.11), and distance of a point from a line gets no section of its own. SB covers all four cases (XII:6.2, 6.3.1, 6.3.2, 6.7).

rulings.subtopic: Foot of Perpendicular, Image, and Projection

stateBoard.note: Foot of perpendicular to a line/plane is worked explicitly in the solved examples and exercises of 6.2/6.7 ('foot of the perpendicular' 15+ mentions), projection in XII:5.3.3. Image of a point is only the doubled-foot corollary — the word 'image' never appears in Ch.6, but every image PYQ reduces to the taught foot construction.

ncert.note: Projection of a vector is taught (XII:10.6.2), but foot of perpendicular and image of a point in 3-D are never demonstrated — the plane sections were deleted, and XII Ch.11's only 'foot of the perpendicular' mention is a passing step inside the skew-line proof. NCERT's mirror-image worked example exists only in 2-D (XI Ch.9).

Skew lines and shortest distance are taught, but there is NO coplanarity-of-two-lines condition ('coplanar' = 3 passing mentions inside the skew-line definition) and no plane-through-intersection work (plane deleted). SB has a dedicated section XII:6.6 Coplanarity of two lines.

rulings.subtopic: Line — Equation, Direction Cosines, and Vector Form

ncert.note: Rationalised NCERT deleted THE PLANE entirely — XII Ch.11 ends at shortest distance between lines; no plane equation in any form (normal, three-point, intercept, plane-through-intersection). 'plane' hits in XII Ch.11 are incidental. A CBSE-taught student meets none of these 47 PYQ's core object.

rulings.subtopic: Tetrahedron Geometry — Centroid, Volume, and Vertices

stateBoard.note: Volume of a tetrahedron via the scalar triple product is taught in 5.5.1 ('tetrahedron' 17 mentions), and the centroid g=(a+b+c+d)/4 is stated with the section formula in 5.2.1.

ncert.note: 'tetrahedron' is ZERO across all NCERT chapters; both triple products were deleted (Ch.10 ends at the cross product), so the volume formula has no basis; and even the 3-D section formula/centroid is gone — rationalised XI Ch.11 keeps only distance between two points.
The Mathematical Reasoning chapter was deleted from rationalised NCERT; no section teaches converse/inverse/contrapositive anywhere in XI or XII.

rulings.subtopic: Negation, Equivalence, Tautology, and Switch Circuits

ncert.note: Mathematical Reasoning was deleted from rationalised NCERT, and switching circuits were never in NCERT even before the rationalisation — this is State-Board-specific material (SB XII:1.5.1–1.5.2).
Mathematical Reasoning deleted from rationalised NCERT; truth tables are taught nowhere in XI/XII.

rulings.subtopic: Mean, Variance, Standard Deviation, and Transformations

ncert.note: Variance/SD are taught in full, but change of origin and scale is only implicit in the shortcut method (SB states it as a result in XI:8.2.3), and combined SD + coefficient of variation are absent — 'coefficient of variation' is ZERO in NCERT vs 17 mentions in SB XI:8.3.1.

rulings.subtopic: Angle, Distance, and Geometry of Pair

ncert.note: NCERT has no pair-of-straight-lines topic in any chapter, before or after rationalisation — 'combined equation' is ZERO across the NCERT corpus (vs 49 mentions in SB XII Ch.4). The angle-of-pair formula tan θ = 2√(h²−ab)/(a+b) has no NCERT source.

rulings.subtopic: Combined Equation and Condition for Pair of Lines

ncert.note: No NCERT chapter teaches homogeneous second-degree equations or the abc+2fgh−af²−bg²−ch²=0 pair condition — 'combined equation' ZERO in NCERT. Entirely State Board material (XII Ch.4).
Geometric counting (chords, triangles from points) appears in the Ch.6 combination examples/exercises — 'chords' has 3 hits in NCERT XI Ch.6.

Linear permutations (incl. repeated objects) and combinations are taught, but circular permutations are absent — 'circular permutation' is ZERO in NCERT vs 8 mentions in SB XI:12.5.4 — so round-table/garland arrangement PYQs have no NCERT source.

rulings.subtopic: Classical Probability, Addition Theorem and Odds

ncert.note: Classical probability and the addition theorem are taught, but ODDS (ratio of complementary probabilities) is never defined — 'odds' is ZERO in NCERT vs 31 mentions in SB, which gives it a dedicated section XI:9.5.

rulings.subtopic: Conditional Probability, Independence and Bayes' Theorem

ncert.note: Cross-year mapping: SB teaches conditional probability/Bayes in Std XI, NCERT in Std XII.

rulings.subtopic: Discrete Random Variables, PMF and CDF

ncert.note: Rationalised NCERT deleted random variables entirely — XII Ch.13 now ends at Bayes' theorem. 'random variable' survives as 5 passing mentions, 'probability mass function' is ZERO (vs 8 in SB XII:14.3.1). Nothing teaches pmf/cdf construction, the core of these 31 PYQ.

Mean/variance of a random variable were deleted with the rest of the random-variable material in the rationalised edition; XII Ch.13 stops at Bayes. 'expected value' has no NCERT teaching occurrence (the XI Ch.12 hits are unrelated limit prose).

rulings.subtopic: Roots — Nature, Vieta's Relations, and Conditions

stateBoard.note: Only the complex-number side is in XI/XII: the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra and solving quadratics with negative discriminant (XI:10.4–10.4.1). Discriminant/nature-of-roots and Vieta's sum-product relations are Class 10 SSC Algebra — 'nature of roots' is ZERO in both XI/XII corpora; 'sum of the roots' hits are incidental (conics/circles).

ncert.note: Rationalised NCERT deleted quadratic-equation theory: XI Ch.4's title still says 'and Quadratic Equations' but no quadratic section survives (spine ends at 4.5 Argand plane). Nature of roots and Vieta's relations are likewise Class 10 material there.

rulings.subtopic: Sequences and Series — AP, HP, Logarithmic and Power Sums

stateBoard.note: The bulk of these PYQs are logarithm-law manipulations — SB teaches product/quotient/power rules AND change of base under the logarithmic function in XI:15.1.5; A.P. (11.2), H.P./means (11.5–11.6) and power series incl. e^x, sin, cos expansions (11.8) cover the rest.

ncert.note: Log laws survive under exponential/logarithmic functions (XII:5.4, incl. change of base), and G.P./A.M.–G.M. remain — but A.P. was relegated to Class 10 by the rationalisation, and H.P., special power sums (Σn², Σn³) and power series are absent entirely.

rulings.subtopic: Inverse, Composite, and Special Function Equations

ncert.note: The inverse/composite tools these PYQs use are taught in both books; the 'special equation' items (e.g. f(x+1)−f(x)=8x+3 with f quadratic) are exercise-level algebra no book section teaches as a topic.

Set operations and Cartesian products are taught, but the practical n(A∪B) counting problems (inclusion-exclusion word problems) were deleted from the rationalised edition — SB states n(A∪B)=n(A)+n(B)−n(A∩B) with worked problems in XI:14.1.3.

rulings.subtopic: Equation of Line — Rotation, Angle, and Bisector

stateBoard.note: Angle between lines, all standard forms incl. normal form, and the locus method (5.1.1) that the bisector PYQs reduce to. Neither book states the two-line angle-bisector FORMULA as a result; SB's 'bisector' mentions are locus-definition examples.

ncert.note: Angle between lines and all line forms taught; right-bisector appears at exercise level. Like SB, no angle-bisector-of-two-lines formula is stated.

rulings.subtopic: Section Formula, Concurrency, Foot of Perpendicular, and Distance

stateBoard.note: Distances (origin/point/parallel lines) in XI:5.4.1–5.4.3, concurrency at exercise level under family of lines (5.4.4); the section formula is taught vectorially in XII:5.2.1 — its 2-D coordinate version is Class 10 SSC. Foot of perpendicular appears in Ch.5 worked examples.

ncert.note: Distance from a line + parallel lines (9.4), concurrency in exercises, and NCERT uniquely works the mirror/image-of-a-point example in Ch.9 (image of P(1,2) in x−3y+4=0 via the perpendicular-bisector argument) — a technique SB never demonstrates in 2-D.

stateBoard.note: Sampled stems are solution-of-triangle (cosine rule from (a+b+c)(a+b−c)=3ab, sides in ratio + area, (cos B+cos C)/(b+c) type) despite sitting in the bank's Trigonometry-I chapter — SB teaches this in XII Ch.3, plus XI:3.5 for A+B+C=π identities.

ncert.note: No sine rule, cosine rule or projection rule anywhere in rationalised NCERT — 'sine rule'/'cosine rule'/'projection rule' are ZERO across the NCERT corpus (vs 12/10/7 SB mentions); the old Sine and Cosine Formulae section was removed from Ch.3, which now ends at compound angles (3.4).

rulings.subtopic: Trig Identities, Compound Angle, and Equations

ncert.note: Identities, allied/compound/multiple angles and factorisation formulas are fully taught in XI:3.3–3.4, but general solutions of trigonometric equations were deleted — 'general solution' is ZERO in NCERT trig (its only hits are the DE chapter) vs 83 mentions in SB XII:3.1.

rulings.subtopic: Inverse Trigonometry — Identities, Equations, and Principal Values

ncert.note: Principal values and basics taught, but the rationalised edition stripped the property toolkit (sum formulas tan-1x+tan-1y, 2tan-1x, sin-1x±sin-1y) that these identity/equation PYQs require; SB XII:3.4.8 carries it in full.

rulings.subtopic: Properties of Triangles — Sine/Cosine Rules and Projection

ncert.note: Rationalised NCERT teaches no solution-of-triangle at all: 'sine rule', 'cosine rule' and 'projection rule' are ZERO in the NCERT corpus; Ch.3 ends at compound-angle formulas. The 52 PYQ here rest entirely on SB XII:3.2–3.3.
Compound, double/triple-angle and product-sum formulas all live in the single section 3.4; half-angle forms appear there as example-level rearrangements.

Collinearity via vector types and components is taught, but the coplanarity test for three vectors is absent — 'coplanar' is ZERO in NCERT XII Ch.10 (vs 51 mentions in SB Ch.5), and its natural tool, the scalar triple product, was deleted.

rulings.subtopic: Scalar Triple Product, Coplanarity, and Volume

ncert.note: Both triple products were deleted from rationalised NCERT — Ch.10 ends at the cross product. No box product, no parallelepiped/tetrahedron volume, no coplanarity application. At 71 PYQ this is the largest single NCERT gap in MHT-CET Maths.
